Listen to this article Share The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has approved the introduction of the CAF U-17 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON), expanding the continental football body’s youth competitions and creating another pathway for the development of women’s football. Advertisement Advertisement The decision was reached on Saturday during a meeting of the Executive Committee in Abuja, Nigeria, chaired by CAF President Patrice Motsepe. The new competition is expected to provide young African female footballers with more opportunities to compete internationally, showcase their talents and gain valuable experience as they progress in their careers. CAF said the tournament reflects its commitment to strengthening women’s football, particularly at the youth level, and developing a stronger pathway for the next generation of African players. Following the approval, the Executive Committee also opened the bidding process for CAF Member Associations interested in hosting the inaugural edition of the competition. The maiden tournament is scheduled to take place in March and April 2028, while the qualifying rounds are expected to begin in April 2027. Interested member associations have three weeks to submit their bids to the CAF Secretariat. Advertisement The introduction of the U-17 competition forms part of CAF’s broader efforts to expand opportunities for young female players, strengthen its women’s football calendar and improve the development of the game across the continent. In a separate decision, CAF also opened the bidding process for the 2028 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON), inviting interested member associations to express their intention to host the tournament.
